Title: TLS Certificate
Description: Open one TLS handshake to a host and port you choose, and see the protocol, the cipher, the expiry and the chain.
Seo_Title: TLS certificate from a live connection | MyDevTools
Keywords: TLS inspect, certificate chain, cipher, expiry, protocol, local agent
PrivacyShort: The check runs on your computer through the local agent. The host, the port and the chain stay on this page.
RememberConnectionHint: The connection is remembered in this browser until the session expires or the agent restarts. Disconnect removes it.
PrivateAllowed: Local network allowed in the agent window
PairCodeHint: Paste the current code from the agent window. The field is cleared after each attempt.
ConnectionNotSaved: This browser could not store the connection or the timeout. They last only until you leave the page.
SetupIntro: Download and start the local agent, then come back to this page.
SetupStep2: Start MyDevTools Agent. For a private or loopback address, turn on “Allow local network and this PC as targets” in the agent window.
SetupStep3: Copy the pairing code from the agent window.
SetupStep4: Paste the code below. If the browser asks for local-network access, allow it for this connection.
PrivacyNote: The browser sends the host, the port and the timeout only to the agent on 127.0.0.1. The agent opens one TLS handshake and closes it without application data. It does not fetch extra certificates. It does not parse a pasted PEM; that stays in the certificate tool. The check does not go to a MyDevTools server. This browser remembers the timeout. It does not store the host, the port or the chain.
NeedTlsCapability: This connection cannot inspect TLS yet. Enter a new pairing code to add tls.inspect. Grants this browser already holds stay until that pairing succeeds.
NotConnected: Connect the local agent before checking a certificate.
HostHint: One host name or IP address. Private and loopback addresses need “Allow local network and this PC as targets” turned on in the agent window. A port range is not accepted.
TimeoutHint: How long to wait for this one connection, from 200 to 10000 milliseconds.
StatusTrusted: {protocol}, {cipher}. The chain is trusted. The leaf expires {expiry}.
StatusUntrusted: {protocol}, {cipher}. The chain is not trusted. The leaf expires {expiry}.
StatusUnreachable: There is no route to that address.
StatusHandshakeFailed: The TCP connection opened, but the TLS handshake failed.
EmptyResult: Check one host and one port to see the protocol, the cipher and the chain.
InvalidInput: Enter one host and one port from 1 to 65535.
InvalidTimeout: Enter a timeout from 200 to 10000 milliseconds.
Error_agent_unavailable: The local agent is not running.
Error_invalid_response: The agent returned a response this page cannot read.
Error_invalid_request: That host, port or timeout was rejected.
Error_unauthorized: The pairing code was rejected, or the session expired.
Error_forbidden: This connection is not allowed to inspect TLS.
Error_pairing_invalid: That pairing code is not the current one.
Error_pairing_expired: That pairing code has expired. Copy the new one from the agent.
Error_pairing_rate_limited: Too many pairing attempts. Wait a minute and try the current code.
Error_unsupported_capability: This agent does not advertise TLS inspect. It needs a build that lists tls.inspect.
Error_busy: The agent is already running as many checks as it allows.
Error_network_error: The request to the local agent failed.
Error_incompatible_protocol: This page and the agent use different protocol versions.
Error_not_found: The agent does not have that request.
Error_name_not_found: That name did not resolve. No connection was opened.
Error_private_network_denied: Private and loopback addresses are blocked. Turn on “Allow local network and this PC as targets” in the agent window.
Error_target_denied: That address is always blocked. Metadata, link-local and multicast addresses cannot be checked.

Seo_Introduction: TLS Certificate asks the local agent to open one TLS handshake to a host and port you type, then closes it without sending application data. The page shows the protocol, the cipher, whether the chain is trusted, when the leaf expires, and each certificate in the chain. The grant is tls.inspect, separate from http.request, icmp.trace, dns.lookup and tcp.connect. Pasted PEM parsing stays in the certificate tool.
Seo_DetailedDescription: The agent resolves the name to the first address and applies the same destination rules as the HTTP client. Private and loopback addresses work only when “Allow local network and this PC as targets” is turned on in the agent window (or the agent was started with --allow-private). Metadata, link-local and multicast addresses stay blocked, and the agent's own listening port is blocked. An untrusted or expired chain is still shown: the handshake signature is checked, and trust is a separate check against the bundled Mozilla roots. The agent does not fetch extra certificates and does not read a banner. A numeric range such as 80-443 is rejected. At most two checks run at once. The timeout stays in this browser. The host, the port and the chain do not.
Seo_Examples:
- `example.com` port 443 shows the protocol, the cipher, the expiry and a trusted chain when the public roots accept it.
- A local self-signed certificate shows a completed handshake with trust off, plus the leaf name and the expiry.
- `80-443` in the host field is rejected. This is not a scan. A pasted PEM stays in the certificate tool.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Start the local agent
Download the agent, start it, and copy the pairing code.

### Step 2: Pair TLS inspect
Paste the code and connect. The page asks for tls.inspect and keeps capabilities this browser already holds.

### Step 3: Check one port
Enter one host and one port, set the timeout, and press Check.

### Step 4: Read the chain
The page shows the protocol, the cipher, trust, the leaf expiry and the chain. Copy it as text. Reloading the page clears it.
Seo_Tips:
- A refused connection, a timeout and a failed handshake are results. They are not a failed check.
- An untrusted chain is still a completed handshake. Trust is reported separately.
- One request is one host and one port. A range stays out of this tool.
- The published Windows download may be older than this page. TLS inspect needs an agent that advertises tls.inspect.
